claim: Two-photon optogenetic stimulation combined with multicellular recording was used to characterize intralaminar and translaminar monosynaptic connections to supragranular (L2/3) neurons in mouse visual cortex.
source: Towards this goal, we combined spatially precise optogenetic stimulation with multicellular recording to deeply characterize intralaminar and translaminar monosynaptic connections to supragranular (L2/3) neurons in the mouse visual cortex.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: Layer 4 excitatory neurons and interneurons within L2/3 represented the most common sources of input to L2/3 pyramidal cells.

evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: L2/3 pyramidal cells receive direct input from dorsal lateral geniculate nucleus (dLGN).

evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: L2/3 neurons in primary visual cortex receive input from higher visual areas.

claim: The L5 to L2/3 connection is most often observed from L5a and therefore thought to originate from intratelencephalic (IT)-type L5 pyramidal neurons.

claim: Feedback projections from anteromedial or lateromedial visual areas preferentially target IT-type L5 neurons in V1 to generate loops between higher and lower visual areas.
source: It was recently demonstrated that feedback projections from anteromedial or lateromedial visual areas preferentially target IT-type L5 neurons in V1 to generate loops between higher and lower visual areas (Young et al., 2021), raising the possibility that local ascending projections from L5 could transmit behavioral or brain-state-related information to superficial layers.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Local ascending projections from L5 could transmit behavioral or brain-state-related information to superficial layers.

source: Consistent with previous reports (Fino and Yuste, 2011; Packer and Yuste, 2011), experiments using AAV-mediated ChrimsonR expression in either Pvalb or Sst interneurons demonstrated a high probability of within-layer inhibitory connectivity that had a steep dependence on the horizontal distance between cells (Figure 6B and C).

evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

source: Interestingly, while the majority of Pvalb to L2/3 PC connections displayed paired-pulse depression, Sst to L2/3 PC connections were approximately linear or facilitated.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: Sst to L2/3 PC connections were approximately linear or facilitated.
source: Interestingly, while the majority of Pvalb to L2/3 PC connections displayed paired-pulse depression, Sst to L2/3 PC connections were approximately linear or facilitated.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: The pattern of paired-pulse dynamics was observed for both intralaminar and translaminar inhibition from the two interneuron subclasses.
source: This pattern was observed for both intralaminar and translaminar inhibition from the two interneuron subclasses and is consistent with previously reported differences in IPSP dynamics according to presynaptic interneuron subclass (Beierlein et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data presented in the study, supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The PPRs measured for Sst to L2/3 FSI connections were significantly smaller than the PPRs measured for Sst to L2/3 PC connections.
source: The PPRs measured for Sst to L2/3 FSI connections were significantly smaller than the PPRs measured for Sst to L2/3 PC connections (p=0.028, post hoc Dunn's; Figure 8C, Figure 8—figure supplement 1), illustrating an example of target-specific synaptic plasticity (Reyes et al., 1998; Blackman et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data presented in the study, with reference to Figure 8C and Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: 96 examples were observed in which multiple presynaptic neurons (up to 12 connections per cell) converged onto individual L2/3 PCs.
source: Two-photon stimulation allowed us to probe up to 75 potential presynaptic partners of a recorded postsynaptic cell – many more than would have been feasible by patch clamping alone – and we observed 96 examples in which multiple presynaptic neurons (up to 12 connections per cell) converged onto individual L2/3 PCs (Figure 9A, also see examples in Figures 2A, 3A, and 4A).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data presented in the study, with reference to Figure 9A.

claim: Out of 10 possible convergence patterns, 2 were significantly more abundant than expected by chance – Rorb to L2/3 PC, and Tlx3 to L2/3 PC.
source: Out of 10 possible convergence patterns (five presynaptic Cre lines to either L2/3 PCs or L2/3 FSIs), 2 were significantly more abundant than expected by chance – Rorb to L2/3 PC, and Tlx3 to L2/3 PC.
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of convergence motifs.

claim: Overrepresentation of convergence motifs was fairly subtle (30–35% more abundant than expected by random connectivity), but highly significant (p<0.001).
source: In both cases, overrepresentation of convergence motifs was fairly subtle (30–35% more abundant than expected by random connectivity), but highly significant (p<0.001) due to the large number of possible two-to-one motifs examined (Rorb: n = 61,911; Tlx3: n = 33,714).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of convergence motifs.

claim: Connections that shared a postsynaptic target displayed either weak or statistically insignificant correlations in PSP amplitudes.
source: Connections that shared a postsynaptic target displayed either weak or statistically insignificant correlations in PSP amplitudes.
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of convergent connections.

claim: There is no evidence that strong synaptic connections (of the classes examined) are biased to particular target cells.
source: Therefore, while the skewed distributions of PSP amplitudes suggest a disproportionate influence of rare and strong synaptic connections (Figure 7A), we do not find evidence that strong synaptic connections (of the classes examined here) are biased to particular target cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the analysis of convergent connections.

claim: 82 photostimulated cells that diverged to 2–4 simultaneously recorded cells in L2/3 were identified across all Cre lines.
source: Across all Cre lines, we identified 82 photostimulated cells that diverged to 2–4 simultaneously recorded cells in L2/3 (Figure 10A, also see examples in Figures 5A and 6A).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data presented in the study, with reference to Figure 10A.

claim: For excitatory Cre lines, the probability of divergence did not vary with total intersomatic distance.
source: It was therefore surprising to find that the probability of divergence did not vary with total intersomatic distance for excitatory Cre lines (Figure 10B; Fisher's exact test; Penk: p=0.29, n = 3/68; Rorb: p=0.43, n = 71/280; Tlx3: p=0.22, n = 16/103; n reported as divergence motifs/motifs in which cell i received a connection, across all distances).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of divergent connections, with reference to Figure 10B.

claim: Single excitatory axons contact L2/3 neurons separated by hundreds of microns.
source: The data illustrate that single excitatory axons contact L2/3 neurons separated by hundreds of microns and argue that excitatory neurons display target specificity beyond spatial proximity.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the analysis of divergent connections.

claim: Excitatory neurons display target specificity beyond spatial proximity.
source: The data illustrate that single excitatory axons contact L2/3 neurons separated by hundreds of microns and argue that excitatory neurons display target specificity beyond spatial proximity.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the analysis of divergent connections.

claim: Both Pvalb and Sst interneurons displayed a decrease in the likelihood of completed divergence as the distance between postsynaptic targets increased.
source: In contrast to excitatory neurons, both Pvalb and Sst interneurons displayed a decrease in the likelihood of completed divergence as the distance between postsynaptic targets increased (Figure 10B; Fisher's exact test; Pvalb: p=0.0014, n = 56/118; Sst: p=0.046, n = 45/114; n reported as divergence motifs/motifs in which cell i received a connection, across all distances).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of divergent connections, with reference to Figure 10B.

claim: Postsynaptic cells near each other were likely to share common input from Pvalb and Sst interneurons (Pj|i > 0.5 at intersomatic distances < 100 µm).
source: Consistent with dense local innervation from inhibitory interneurons (Karnani et al., 2014), postsynaptic cells near each other were likely to share common input from Pvalb and Sst interneurons (Pj|i > 0.5 at intersomatic distances < 100 µm).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of divergent connections, supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The relatively high, but distance-dependent, probability of inhibitory divergence suggests that the outgoing connectivity of interneurons is less selective than the output of excitatory neurons.
source: The relatively high, but distance-dependent, probability of inhibitory divergence suggests that the outgoing connectivity of interneurons is less selective than the output of excitatory neurons.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the analysis of divergent connections.

claim: Interneurons can connect to widely distributed targets as examples were observed in which postsynaptic cells more than 200 µm apart shared divergent inhibitory input from the same interneuron.
source: However, the data additionally illustrate that interneurons can connect to widely distributed targets as we observed examples in which postsynaptic cells more than 200 µm apart shared divergent inhibitory input from the same interneuron.
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of divergent connections.

claim: For Penk and Rorb-labeled neurons within L2/3, the probability of completed divergence was between 4% and 5%.
source: For Penk and Rorb-labeled neurons within L2/3, the probability of completed divergence was between 4% and 5% (Figure 10C) – similar to the connection probability measured across all tested intralaminar inputs to L2/3 PCs (Figures 3B and 5B).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of divergent connections, with reference to Figure 10C.

claim: The number of observed divergence motifs measured using the Penk-Cre line was consistent with a random network.
source: Accordingly, the number of observed divergence motifs measured using the Penk-Cre line was consistent with a random network (Figure 10—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of divergence motifs, with reference to Figure 10—figure supplement 1.

claim: For translaminar excitatory connections (from Rorb or Tlx3-labeled cells), the probability of completed divergence was two- to threefold higher than the corresponding connection probabilities measured across all tested connections.
source: By contrast, for translaminar excitatory connections (from Rorb or Tlx3-labeled cells), the probability of completed divergence was two- to threefold higher than the corresponding connection probabilities measured across all tested connections (Figure 10C).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of divergent connections, with reference to Figure 10C.

claim: The numbers of observed divergence motifs from Rorb and Tlx3 neurons were dramatically and significantly greater than predicted by a random network.
source: Additionally, the numbers of observed divergence motifs from Rorb and Tlx3 neurons were dramatically and significantly greater than predicted by a random network (L4 Rorb: p<0.001, L5 Rorb: p=0.004; L5 Tlx3: p=0.007; Figure 10—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of divergence motifs, with reference to Figure 10—figure supplement 1.

claim: Divergence from inhibitory interneurons was also overrepresented, and this was especially true for translaminar inhibition from both Pvalb and Sst interneurons.
source: Divergence from inhibitory interneurons was also overrepresented, and this was especially true for translaminar inhibition from both Pvalb and Sst interneurons (Figure 10C, Figure 10—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of divergence motifs, with reference to Figure 10C and Figure 10—figure supplement 1.

claim: Data from both excitatory and inhibitory Cre lines suggest the existence of subsets of photostimulated neurons in L4 and L5 that mediate translaminar synaptic connections to L2/3.
source: Data from both excitatory and inhibitory Cre lines suggest the existence of subsets of photostimulated neurons in L4 and L5 that mediate translaminar synaptic connections to L2/3.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the analysis of divergent connections.

claim: Subsets of cells in L4 and L5 likely target a greater number of neurons within L2/3 than predicted by the overall measured connection probabilities.
source: By extension, these subsets of cells in L4 and L5 likely target a greater number of neurons within L2/3 than predicted by the overall measured connection probabilities.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the analysis of divergent connections.

claim: No significant correlations were observed when examining PSP amplitudes from single Rorb, Tlx3, or Pvalb neurons onto multiple L2/3 PCs.
source: We did not observe significant correlations when examining PSP amplitudes from single Rorb, Tlx3, or Pvalb neurons onto multiple L2/3 PCs (Rorb: R = –0.25, p=0.17, n = 32; Tlx3: R = –0.46, p=0.30, n = 7; Pvalb: R = 0.07, p=0.77, n = 19, Pearson's R in log-space).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of divergent connections.

claim: A moderate positive correlation was found in the amplitudes of synaptic responses measured from diverging Sst interneurons (Sst: R = 0.52, p=0.016, n = 21).
source: However, we found a moderate positive correlation in the amplitudes of synaptic responses measured from diverging Sst interneurons (Figure 10D; Sst: R = 0.52, p=0.016, n = 21).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of divergent connections, with reference to Figure 10D.

claim: The effective strength of connections generated by a single presynaptic neuron onto its targets can vary substantially.
source: In total, the data demonstrate that the effective strength of connections generated by a single presynaptic neuron onto its targets can vary substantially, but also provide evidence that some Sst neurons more strongly inhibit their local network than others.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the analysis of divergent connections.

claim: Some Sst neurons more strongly inhibit their local network than others.
source: In total, the data demonstrate that the effective strength of connections generated by a single presynaptic neuron onto its targets can vary substantially, but also provide evidence that some Sst neurons more strongly inhibit their local network than others.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the analysis of divergent connections.

claim: Intralaminar excitatory connections from Penk-labeled neurons in L2/3 displayed a strong bias for FSIs over PCs in terms of connectivity and unitary connection strength.
source: For example, intralaminar excitatory connections from Penk-labeled neurons in L2/3 displayed a strong bias for FSIs over PCs in terms of connectivity (Figure 3B) and unitary connection strength (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data presented in the study, with reference to Figures 3B and 7B.

claim: FFI may be engaged following excitatory neuron activity within layers 2/3, 4, or 5, but will be most robustly recruited by activity within L2/3 due to the abundance and strength of intralaminar excitatory inputs to L2/3 FSIs.
source: Our measurements of excitatory inputs to L2/3 FSIs and L2/3 PCs suggest that FFI may be engaged following excitatory neuron activity within layers 2/3, 4, or 5, but will be most robustly recruited by activity within L2/3 due to the abundance and strength of intralaminar excitatory inputs to L2/3 FSIs.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data on excitatory connectivity to FSIs.

claim: Strong intralaminar FFI could promote sparse coding by L2/3 PCs and contribute to feature competition among L2/3 PCs.
source: Strong intralaminar FFI could promote sparse coding by L2/3 PCs and contribute to feature competition among L2/3 PCs, wherein the activity of one L2/3 PC reduces the activity of similarly tuned neighbors (Chettih and Harvey, 2019).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential function of intralaminar FFI, supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Differences in the strength, kinetics, and dynamics of inhibitory signaling likely impart diverse computational functions to inhibitory interneuron subclasses.
source: Differences in the strength, kinetics, and dynamics of inhibitory signaling likely impart diverse computational functions to inhibitory interneuron subclasses (Abbott and Regehr, 2004; Silver, 2010).
evidence: This is a general statement about the functional implications of inhibitory diversity, supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Differences between Pvalb and Sst connection properties were found for both intralaminar and translaminar connections.
source: As differences between Pvalb and Sst connection properties were found for both intralaminar and translaminar connections (Figure 7E and C), our data suggest that horizontal and vertical and inhibition from an interneuron subclass may serve similar computational functions.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data presented in the study, with reference to Figures 7E and C.

claim: Horizontal and vertical inhibition from an interneuron subclass may serve similar computational functions.
source: As differences between Pvalb and Sst connection properties were found for both intralaminar and translaminar connections (Figure 7E and C), our data suggest that horizontal and vertical and inhibition from an interneuron subclass may serve similar computational functions.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data on inhibitory connectivity.

claim: The properties of synaptic connections are influenced, but are far from fully determined, by presynaptic and postsynaptic cell identity.
source: Therefore, the properties of synaptic connections are influenced, but are far from fully determined, by presynaptic and postsynaptic cell identity.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data showing diversity within and overlap across subclasses.

claim: There is a retinotopic map of visual space that is conserved across layers in V1.
source: There is a retinotopic map of visual space that is conserved across layers in V1 – arguing for strong vertical synaptic connections (Dräger, 1975; Mangini and Pearlman, 1980; Wagor et al., 1980; Schuett et al., 2002; Bonin et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Rodent V1 lacks the smoothly varying orientation columns observed in higher mammals.
source: Rodent V1 lacks the smoothly varying orientation columns observed in higher mammals (Grinvald et al., 1986; Hübener et al., 1997; Ts'o et al., 1990); instead, neurons with disparate orientation tuning are intermingled in a 'salt and pepper' fashion (Ohki et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Neurons with disparate orientation tuning are intermingled in a 'salt and pepper' fashion in rodent V1.
source: Rodent V1 lacks the smoothly varying orientation columns observed in higher mammals (Grinvald et al., 1986; Hübener et al., 1997; Ts'o et al., 1990); instead, neurons with disparate orientation tuning are intermingled in a 'salt and pepper' fashion (Ohki et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Nearby cells display more similar tuning than those farther away from each other.
source: However, it is reported that nearby cells display more similar tuning than those farther away from each other (Ringach et al., 2016) and that local biases in orientation tuning reveal a global map in orientation tuning that spans V1 and neighboring visual areas (Fahey et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Local biases in orientation tuning reveal a global map in orientation tuning that spans V1 and neighboring visual areas.
source: However, it is reported that nearby cells display more similar tuning than those farther away from each other (Ringach et al., 2016) and that local biases in orientation tuning reveal a global map in orientation tuning that spans V1 and neighboring visual areas (Fahey et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Connections with little horizontal offset may preserve or stabilize functional maps, while connections between more horizontally distributed neurons may promote their reorganization.
source: Connections with little horizontal offset may preserve or stabilize functional maps, while connections between more horizontally distributed neurons may promote their reorganization.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential function of connections with different spatial distributions.

claim: The highest rate of excitatory neuron connectivity to L2/3 PCs was observed from L4 Rorb-labeled neurons with 0–100 µm of horizontal offset.
source: In our study, the highest rate of excitatory neuron connectivity to L2/3 PCs was observed from L4 Rorb-labeled neurons with 0–100 µm of horizontal offset (Figure 5D) – a likely means of preserving the retinotopic map established by inputs from dLGN.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data presented in the study, with reference to Figure 5D.

claim: The highest rate of excitatory neuron connectivity to L2/3 PCs from L4 Rorb-labeled neurons with 0–100 µm of horizontal offset is a likely means of preserving the retinotopic map established by inputs from dLGN.
source: In our study, the highest rate of excitatory neuron connectivity to L2/3 PCs was observed from L4 Rorb-labeled neurons with 0–100 µm of horizontal offset (Figure 5D) – a likely means of preserving the retinotopic map established by inputs from dLGN.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data on excitatory connectivity.

claim: The falloff in connection rate with horizontal distance was gradual for all classes of translaminar excitatory inputs to L2/3 PCs measured in this study.
source: However, the falloff in connection rate with horizontal distance was gradual for all classes of translaminar excitatory inputs to L2/3 PCs measured in this study (Figure 5D, Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data presented in the study, with reference to Figure 5D and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: The convergence and divergence of connections across hundreds of microns of horizontal space illustrate putative circuit mechanisms by which translaminar excitatory connections can promote both the maintenance and redistribution of sensory information across layers.
source: These findings, and the convergence and divergence of connections across hundreds of microns of horizontal space (Figures 8 and 9), illustrate putative circuit mechanisms by which translaminar excitatory connections can promote both the maintenance and redistribution of sensory information across layers.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data on excitatory connectivity.

claim: Excitatory input from L5 IT neurons to L2/3 PCs rivals excitation from L4 IT neurons in terms of connection probability.
source: We found that excitatory input from L5 IT neurons (labeled by either Rorb or Tlx3-Cre) to L2/3 PCs rivals excitation from L4 IT neurons (labeled by either Rorb or Scnn1a-Cre) in terms of connection probability (Figures 5B and 4D), unitary connection strength (Figure 7), as well as convergence and divergence (Figures 9 and 10).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data presented in the study, with reference to multiple figures.

claim: Excitatory input from L5 IT neurons to L2/3 PCs rivals excitation from L4 IT neurons in terms of unitary connection strength.
source: We found that excitatory input from L5 IT neurons (labeled by either Rorb or Tlx3-Cre) to L2/3 PCs rivals excitation from L4 IT neurons (labeled by either Rorb or Scnn1a-Cre) in terms of connection probability (Figures 5B and 4D), unitary connection strength (Figure 7), as well as convergence and divergence (Figures 9 and 10).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data presented in the study, with reference to multiple figures.

claim: Excitatory input from L5 IT neurons to L2/3 PCs rivals excitation from L4 IT neurons in terms of convergence and divergence.
source: We found that excitatory input from L5 IT neurons (labeled by either Rorb or Tlx3-Cre) to L2/3 PCs rivals excitation from L4 IT neurons (labeled by either Rorb or Scnn1a-Cre) in terms of connection probability (Figures 5B and 4D), unitary connection strength (Figure 7), as well as convergence and divergence (Figures 9 and 10).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data presented in the study, with reference to multiple figures.

claim: In vivo studies demonstrate a strong influence of brain state and active behavior on the activity of neurons in primary visual cortex.
source: The connection from L5 IT neurons to L2/3 PCs is interesting in the context of in vivo studies demonstrating a strong influence of brain state and active behavior on the activity of neurons in primary visual cortex (Niell and Stryker, 2010; Keller et al., 2012; Neske et al., 2019; Stringer et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: If L5 IT neurons receive long-range input encoding behavioral variables from higher cortical areas, local projections from L5 IT neurons could provide a mechanism to distribute this information within V1.
source: If L5 IT neurons receive long-range input encoding behavioral variables from higher cortical areas, local projections from L5 IT neurons could provide a mechanism to distribute this information within V1 so that it can be integrated with synaptic connections providing sensory information (e.g., thalamic input or connections ascending from L4).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential function of L5 IT to L2/3 connections.

claim: The age range of animals used in this study is older than most previous studies.
source: The age range of animals used in this study is older than most, and connectivity in younger animals may be more specifically driven by sensory input.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental design and a speculation about potential age-related differences.

claim: Connectivity in younger animals may be more specifically driven by sensory input.
source: The age range of animals used in this study is older than most, and connectivity in younger animals may be more specifically driven by sensory input.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential age-related differences in connectivity.

claim: The use of Tlx3 and Rorb-Cre allowed more thorough identification and measurement of L5 to L2/3 connections that may be specific to IT-type L5 neurons.
source: It is also possible that the use of Tlx3 and Rorb-Cre allowed us to more thoroughly identify and measure these somewhat rare connections that may be specific to IT-type L5 neurons rather than the primarily subcortical-projecting extratelencephalic (ET)-type L5 neurons.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the advantages of the genetic labeling approach used in the study.

claim: Imparting photosensitivity to genetically defined subclasses of neurons can provide additional insight into the source of photostimulus responses not achieved with one-photon or two-photon glutamate uncaging.
source: More generally, imparting photosensitivity to genetically defined subclasses of neurons can provide additional insight into the source of photostimulus responses not achieved with one-photon or two-photon glutamate uncaging.
evidence: This is a statement about the advantages of the optogenetic approach used in the study.

claim: Connections arising from unlabeled populations of cells cannot be tested using optogenetic approaches.
source: However, connections arising from unlabeled populations of cells cannot be tested.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the optogenetic approach used in the study.

claim: Glutamate uncaging may allow less biased measures of connectivity due to the ubiquitous expression of glutamate receptors.
source: Glutamate uncaging may allow less biased measures of connectivity due to the ubiquitous expression of glutamate receptors, but the higher density of photosensitive neurons may result in greater off-target activation and subsequent false positives, even with spatially refined two-photon stimulation (Figure 2D–I).
evidence: This is a statement about the advantages and disadvantages of glutamate uncaging compared to optogenetics.

claim: Up to 15% of photostimulated neurons did not generate APs due to variability between cells within a Cre line.
source: We endeavored to account for these differences by calibrating photostimulation power according to the Cre line used; however, due to variability between cells within a Cre line, we estimate that up to 15% of photostimulated neurons did not generate APs (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data presented in the study, with reference to Figure 1B.

claim: Even low variability in AP timing may preclude detection of weak and/or unreliable connections.
source: Additionally, while the timing of two-photon-evoked spiking in response to repeated photostimulation was highly consistent for most ChrimsonR-expressing cells (jitter < 1 ms; Figure 1C), even low variability in AP timing may preclude detection of weak and/or unreliable connections.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the optogenetic approach used in the study.

claim: Sources of false negatives are strongly mitigated in paired recordings where variability in timing, or failure to evoke presynaptic APs by current injection, can be corrected using AP detection and alignment of postsynaptic responses.
source: These sources of false negatives are strongly mitigated in paired recordings where variability in timing, or failure to evoke presynaptic APs by current injection, can be corrected using AP detection and alignment of postsynaptic responses.
evidence: This is a statement about the advantages of paired recordings compared to optogenetics.

claim: Photostimulation can generate spiking in off-target presynaptic cells that also express the opsin, leading to false positives when measuring connectivity.
source: The spatial resolution of our photostimulation protocol approached, but did not reach, the dimensions of an individual neuron (Figure 1D). Therefore, photostimulation can generate spiking in off-target presynaptic cells that also express the opsin, leading to false positives when measuring connectivity.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the optogenetic approach used in the study.

claim: Experiments in which optically identified presynaptic cells were subsequently patched demonstrated that off-target activation occurs, but suggested that it was rare under the experimental conditions.
source: Experiments in which we subsequently patched optically identified presynaptic cells (Figure 4, Figure 4—figure supplement 1) demonstrated that this occurs, but suggested that it was rare under our experimental conditions (11 verified excitatory connections in 12 tested, 22 verified inhibitory connections in 22 tested).
evidence: This is a finding from the validation experiments, with reference to Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Connection probabilities estimated by two-photon stimulation and paired recordings were not statistically different.
source: Connection probabilities estimated by each method were not statistically different.
evidence: This is a finding from the comparison of two-photon optogenetics data to paired recordings.

claim: Measurements of synaptic connectivity made at the population level using photostimulation accurately represent the underlying connectivity.
source: Altogether, the results argue that while photostimulation carries sources of error not present in paired recordings, measurements of synaptic connectivity made at the population level accurately represent the underlying connectivity.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the validation experiments comparing two-photon optogenetics to paired recordings.

claim: A source of false negatives inherent to acute slice preparations is the severing of neuronal processes.
source: A source of false negatives inherent to acute slice preparations is the severing of neuronal processes.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of acute slice preparations.

claim: Connection probabilities measured in vitro may be thought of as the lower bounds for connection probabilities present in vivo.
source: This subject has been explored in other studies, and in this context, connection probabilities measured in vitro may be thought of as the lower bounds for connection probabilities present in vivo (Stepanyants et al., 2009; Levy and Reyes, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Slices were cut at a slightly oblique angle to preserve neuronal processes.
source: In this study, slices were cut at a slightly oblique angle to preserve neuronal processes, and we targeted patching and photostimulation to cells that were >40 µm below the surface of the slice (both cells were >40 µm deep for 81.9% of connections probed).
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: Connections were observed from L5 IT-type neurons to distant L2/3 neurons with 300–600 µm of horizontal offset – corresponding to total intersomatic distances of 485–744 µm (11 connections/506 probed, 2.2%).
source: We observed connections from L5 IT-type neurons (labeled by Rorb or Tlx3-Cre) to distant L2/3 neurons with 300–600 µm of horizontal offset – corresponding to total intersomatic distances of 485–744 µm (11 connections/506 probed, 2.2%).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: The near absence of connections observed over similar intersomatic distances from Sst neurons with >200 µm of horizontal offset or from Ntsr1 neurons indicates selectivity of the connections and is not strictly a result of acute slice preparation.
source: Considering this, we believe the near absence of connections observed over similar intersomatic distances (e.g., from Sst neurons with >200 µm of horizontal offset or from Ntsr1 neurons) indicates selectivity of the connections and is not strictly a result of acute slice preparation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data on connectivity.

claim: Intersomatic distance is not equivalent to the distance an axon travels to form a synaptic contact.
source: However, we acknowledge that intersomatic distance is not equivalent to the distance an axon travels to form a synaptic contact (e.g., synapses formed on the distal dendrites of a nearby postsynaptic cell), and some presynaptic projections may be more prone to cutting than others due to tortuous axon trajectories.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of using intersomatic distance as a measure of axonal distance.

claim: Features measured in the acute slice preparation may differ in vivo due to differences in ionic gradients and the dynamic influence of neuromodulators.
source: The effect of a synaptic connection on the postsynaptic membrane potential is influenced by multiple complex biological mechanisms including presynaptic transmitter release, postsynaptic receptor activation, and the intrinsic electrophysiological properties of the cell. Features measured in the acute slice preparation may differ in vivo due to differences in ionic gradients and the dynamic influence of neuromodulators.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of acute slice preparations.

claim: The effect of a distal synaptic connection on its local postsynaptic compartment may be drastically different than the response measured by a somatic recording, and such connections may go undetected.
source: Furthermore, the effect of a distal synaptic connection on its local postsynaptic compartment may be drastically different than the response measured by a somatic recording, and such connections may go undetected.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of somatic recordings.

claim: Recording of postsynaptic responses in either voltage- or current-clamp each comes with inherent advantages and disadvantages.
source: To this end, recording of postsynaptic responses in either voltage- or current-clamp each comes with inherent advantages and disadvantages (Williams and Mitchell, 2008; Barth et al., 2016; Jiang et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Voltage-clamp recording is generally thought to increase the ability to detect small responses.
source: Although voltage-clamp recording is generally thought to increase the ability to detect small responses (especially when combined with pharmacology to partially isolate synaptic currents), it presents challenges in the interpretation of results due to space-clamp errors, and strong somatic bias has been shown to persist under nominally ideal recording conditions (Spruston et al., 1993; Williams and Mitchell, 2008; Beaulieu-Laroche and Harnett, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Voltage-clamp recording presents challenges in the interpretation of results due to space-clamp errors.
source: Although voltage-clamp recording is generally thought to increase the ability to detect small responses (especially when combined with pharmacology to partially isolate synaptic currents), it presents challenges in the interpretation of results due to space-clamp errors, and strong somatic bias has been shown to persist under nominally ideal recording conditions (Spruston et al., 1993; Williams and Mitchell, 2008; Beaulieu-Laroche and Harnett, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Current-clamp recordings were used to conduct this survey of synaptic connectivity and functional properties.
